summary: Chitai Takenaka is an Indologist and philosopher who studied at Kyoto University until 1968. He served as an assistant professor at Hanazono University (attested 1979–1983) and later as a professor at Tokoha Gakuen University (attested 1989).
Chiyong Kim is a Buddhist studies scholar who held professorships attested in 1976 at both International Buddhist University and Shitennoji Junior College.

Chizen Akanuma was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Otani University, where he later became a professor in 1919, and at Kōkōdō under Manshi Kiyozawa in 1909. He also founded the Eastern Buddhist Society in 1921.

Chizuko Yoshimizu specializes in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. She studied at Gakushuin University, the University of Tokyo under Zuiho Yamaguchi, and earned her doctorate at the University of Vienna. She was later appointed professor at the University of Tsukuba in 2011.

Chlodwig H. Werba is a scholar of Indology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He served as a professor at the University of Vienna, where his faculty affiliation is attested between 1990 and 2022.
Chogye Shabdrung is a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Sakya College in 2003 under Khenchen Sonam Gyatso.

Chogye Trichen Rinpoche was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology figure who studied under teachers including Geshe Tsechok, Kunga Chophel, and Zimwok Rinpoche. In 1928, he became the Eighteenth Chogye Trichen at Nalendra Monastery.
Chogyū Takayama worked in philosophy and Japanology. He was educated at Fukushima Prefectural Asaka High School and studied at the University of Tokyo from circa 1893 to 1896.
Chokgyur Dechen Lingpa was a 19th-century Tibetan Buddhist figure who studied under Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo and Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye, whom he also taught.
Chong Go is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Dongguk University and under the traditional teacher Daehaeng Kun Sunim.
Chris Clark is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who completed a PhD under Mark Allon at the University of Sydney by 2015, where he served as an honorary associate as attested in 2019.

Christian Bartholomae specialized in Iranian and Central Asian studies, linguistics, and Indology. He studied under Heinrich Hübschmann and held professorships at Halle-Wittenberg, Münster, Giessen, and Heidelberg between 1879 and 1924.

Christian Bernert is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the International Buddhist Academy and the University of Vienna, where he completed his master's degree under Klaus-Dieter Mathes.

Christian Coseru is a scholar of philosophy, Indology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Bucharest and the Australian National University under Jay L. Garfield and John Powers. He became an associate professor of philosophy at the College of Charleston.

Christian Gottlob Heyne was a German scholar of linguistics and history and archaeology. After earning a master's at the University of Leipzig, he served as a professor at the University of Göttingen from 1763 and library director from 1764 to 1812.

Christian Haskett specializes in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He completed a PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison, having studied under Robert A. F. Thurman and Lobsang Jamspal, and held a post at Washington and Lee University attested in 2010.

Christian K. Wedemeyer works in Buddhist, religious, and Indological studies. He earned an MA and PhD at Columbia University under Robert A. F. Thurman, taught at the University of Copenhagen, and became a professor at the University of Chicago.

Christian Karl Josias von Bunsen was a scholar of religious studies and linguistics. He studied under Christian Gottlob Heyne at Göttingen and Antoine-Isaac Silvestre de Sacy, later serving as Prussian envoy from circa 1823 to 1854.

Christian Lassen was an Indologist and linguist who studied under August Wilhelm von Schlegel at the University of Bonn. He became a Privatdozent at Bonn in 1830 and served as professor of Old Indian language and literature from 1840 to 1876.

Christian Lee Novetzke is a scholar of Indology, religious studies, and history. He studied at Macalester College, Harvard Divinity School, and Columbia University, holding posts as professor at the University of Pennsylvania (2003–2007) and the University of Washington (from 2007).
